title: The Drowned Veil
premise: Theo Nystrom, exiled for refusing to weaponize their storm-calling, hides among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things—until a prophecy written a century ago names tonight as the night the Veiled King devours his city. The 'thing wearing the crown' is a drowned god bound to the royal bloodline, fed by oaths of loyalty that have curdled into possession. Theo must choose between exposing the guild's complicity in the binding and saving the king's estranged daughter, Sera, whose love for a common soldier makes her the one oath the god cannot digest. In the end, Theo breaks their own exile-oath—the last thread anchoring the god—and calls the storm they swore never to call again, drowning the crown and crowning Sera in its place.
about_author: Kestrel Quintana is a former archivist who spent six years cataloging maritime folklore before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat on a rain-dark coast, where the weather is treated as a co-author.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While reconciling the guild's ledgers, Theo finds their own name and today's date in a century-old prophetic text the guild was paid to suppress. Their mentor admits the guild has known about the Veiled King for generations—and sold the knowledge of how to bind him. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering invisibility was always someone else's arrangement.

chapters.title: What the Oaths Weigh
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Theo and Sera. Theo infiltrates the palace under cover of an audit and witnesses the king speaking in two voices; Sera, chafing under her father's increasingly inhuman decrees, meets Theo and recognizes a fellow prisoner of duty. Together they trace the binding to the coronation oaths themselves. Emotional beat: wary alliance kindling into trust.

chapters.title: The God Below the Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, with Theo present. The drowned god, aware it has been found, forces the king to declare martial law and demand Sera swear the succession oath at dawn—which would complete the binding forever. The guild offers Theo reinstatement and their exile lifted if they let the ceremony proceed. Emotional beat: betrayal at the moment of greatest need; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Storm-Called
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the dawn ceremony, Theo publicly breaks their exile-oath, unbinding themselves and loosening the god's anchor, then calls the storm they were exiled for refusing to wield. The god drowns back into the deep; the king dies human; Sera refuses the crown's old form and refounds the monarchy on chosen, revocable vows. Emotional beat: costly liberation—truth over loyalty, love over power.
